The verify job eval expands three hardcoded gate names whose values are job-result env enums.

local_checks.invariant: Registry and provision contracts must not embed a registry token or grant a secret plane.

A secret-classified provision row is rejected when it carries an expected value or a non-secret Cloudflare plane. Env catalog and onboarding metadata describe names and planes; they do not authorize a caller.

local_checks.result: api-keys.post.ts normalizes scopes, then for authMethod api-key calls findScopesBeyondCaller before insert and returns 403 on any refused scope. A caller holding * is unbounded; a caller with any other scope that requests none is refused as an unscoped mint; each requested scope absent from the held set, including *, is refused. An empty held set can mint only another empty set, which is the same unscoped credential and still cannot mint named scopes or *. resolveApiKeyMintExpiry then refuses a * key with null expiry or more than 90 days. boundChildApiKeyExpiry refuses an explicit child expiry past a parent that expires and clamps an omitted expiry to the parent. Session callers skip the ceiling because the session is the user credential; * minted that way is still lifetime-capped. The insert stores serializeApiKeyScopes of that same normalized list and the raw key is returned once.

local_checks.invariant: A local email setup or reset link is a single-use SHA-256 of a 32-byte token, bound to purpose and address. Setup is issued only for an allowlisted address with no user. WHERE tokenHash matches, consumedAt is null, and expiresAt is in the future, RETURNING the row. A missing row, a purpose other than setup or reset, a setup address no longer allowlisted, or a reset with no user is rejected after the consume, so the link cannot be retried. Context-bound proofs omit installationId because the cloud mints it; the library compares the other signed fields to the session and verifies against the recorded key, not a caller-supplied key. local_checks.invariant: A route guard accepts only a bearer whose digest matches an active session of the required credential class. Revoke and rotate end the affected sessions in the same batch as the credential change. The session row id is not a bearer.

README states the bearer is the secret and the session id is not. revokeDeviceAtomically and rotateCredentialAtomically revoke sessions in one batch; rotate filters to the rotated credential class. devices-session.test.ts expects the other class to remain and the ingest heartbeat to report stale. That class split is the documented control, not a missed revoke. The guard does not re-read device generation because the batch already revoked the sessions of the affected class.

local_checks.invariant: completeClaim must not charge the owner's claim token until the caller's org and resource match the token. completeClaimWithRecordedApproval has no caller org; ceremony failures on that path are counted against the shared token subject on purpose. local_checks.result: completeClaim sets callerScopeMatches to org-and-resource match. When that is false, runCompleteClaim records only the caller's account and IP subjects and returns unauthorized_user, which is the #533 control. completeClaimWithRecordedApproval sets callerScopeMatches to a function that returns true, so hardware_mismatch and the other completionBlocker refusals are recorded against token.tokenHash. That digest is the same sha256 startClaim stores and checks. Five failures in 900 seconds lock the token for 900 seconds, including a later startClaim. devices-claim-completion.test.ts names this shared lockout and states that locking the rightful device is the point of the counter. README scopes the do-not-charge-until-org-match rule to completeClaim and says startClaim and completion share the token counter to bound guessing. The session id is a UUID and is not treated as a secret, but spending the ceremony budget is the control the package tests. Without deviceProof the interface comment requires the caller to verify the request first; reissueOnIdempotentReplay without a proof throws invalid before any credential is issued; a proof-less race loser does not receive deviceId. Account and IP subjects are namespaced by purpose; token and device subjects are intentionally not.

local_checks.invariant: GET and HEAD /images/** are public by the package's stated model. Object helpers that accept a caller-chosen key do not authorize, and the package says the caller must scope them.
local_checks.result: The image handler is defineEventHandler with no session check. README states the route is public, that a key outside every prefix is 404 before R2, and that uploadToR2, deleteFromR2, and readR2AsBase64 do not decide who may use a key. local_checks.invariant: The public upload route stores only bytes whose magic matches the raster allow-list, under a server-generated key, and never under a client filename or client Content-Type.
local_checks.result: POST requires Content-Length, caps the body, and calls validateUploadFiles before sniffing. sniffUploadImageType returns image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, or image/avif, or empty. An empty sniff is 415 and nothing is written. The stored key is uploads/ plus crypto.randomUUID plus the extension of the sniffed type. The client filename is not used as a key. uploadToR2 itself does not validate content type; the route passes the sniffed type. A direct caller of uploadToR2 can write another prefix or type, and README says the serve path still allow-lists type.

local_checks.invariant: The image route reads R2 only with the same slug that matched a configured prefix, and it will not stream a content type outside the raster allow-list.
local_checks.result: getRouterParam supplies slug. prefixes.find uses startsWith, and a miss is 404 before r2.get or r2.head. There is no second decode between that check and the storage call. The module rejects an empty prefix at setup because it would serve the bucket. The default prefix is uploads/. contentTypeFor uses the extension map only when typeFromExtension is set and the extension is in EXTENSION_TYPES; otherwise it uses the stored type. isAllowedUploadContentType then requires one of the five rasters, and the response sets X-Content-Type-Options nosniff. R2 keys are not filesystem paths, so a dot-dot segment does not escape the prefix. The prefix is not required to end with a delimiter. GET does not re-sniff the object bytes.

local_checks.result: install-swift-linux.py downloads a pinned swift.org tarball, imports that vendor's all-keys.asc, verifies the detached signature, and extracts with tarfile filter data before the compile smoke. No in-repo key fingerprint is pinned; that vendor-root gap is hardening. refresh-generator-pins.mjs reads a local workflows checkout with git and rewrites only the generator pin, history, and changeset. It does not execute workflow files or publish.
